tagline: These halls used to be filled with laughter
title: The long table
journal:
I counted the chairs again, twenty-two. Nobody sits in them now but the steward still has them dusted on a Sunday, which I think is for my benefit more than the chairs.

There is a scorch mark near the far end where my brother knocked a candle over the winter he came home with a beard he was far too proud of. The rug never quite recovered. I used to tell the staff to replace it and now I would have them hanged if they tried. Not really. But I would be cross.

The fire is too big for one person. I keep it that way anyway. Somebody has to keep the place warm in case anyone comes back, and if they do, I would rather they found me here than somewhere sensible.

- R
prompt: very High up in the rafters of a castle hall, looking down into a grand hall, a roaring fire illuminates a brooding tall figure at the head of a long and empty dining table.
